basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 22.' and it opens '(Vers. 22.) Et fuerunt filii Lothan, Chorri et Aemam: et soror Lothan Thamna. Haec est'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 22.) Et fuerunt filii Lothan, Chorri et Aemam: et soror Lothan Thamna. Haec est Thamna, de qua supra dictum est. Et Thamna erat concubina Eliphaz filii primogeniti Esau, et ex ipsa natus est Amalech. Idcirco autem Chorraeorum recordatus est, quia primogenitus filiorum Esau ex filiabus eorum acceperat concubinam. Quod autem dicitur, Theman et Cenez et Amalech, et reliqua: sciamus postea regionibus Idumaeorum ex his vocabula imposita.
